key_insight: Instead of saving successful experiences as text, AgentFactory records them as executable subagent code and continuously refines those subagents via execution feedback, enabling reliable re‑execution and composition for complex tasks.
problem_solved: Current LLM-agent self-evolution stores solutions as textual prompts/reflections that are brittle and hard to re-run or compose reliably in complex, stateful scenarios; AgentFactory addresses reproducibility, reliability, and reuse.
method: Encode successful task solutions as executable subagents (small, testable code modules) rather than textual memories or prompts.
Accumulate and manage a library/registry of subagents for selection, composition, and reuse across new tasks.
Continuously validate and refine subagents using execution feedback (automated test runs, failure-triggered edits, and performance-driven updates).
impact: Makes LLM-based agents more reproducible, debuggable, and scalable by turning experience into reusable, executable components—improving reliability on complex workflows and enabling easier transfer and composition of capabilities.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Task → generate subagent code → execute → feedback loop → refine & store in registry
Side-by-side comparison: textual-prompt approach vs executable-subagent approach with reliability/outcome bars
Modular library graphic: stack of composable code modules (subagents) being assembled into a higher-level agent
Line chart or bar chart: success rate or task completion improving across iterations as subagents accumulate and are refined
paper_title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse
paper_authors: Zhang Zhang, Shuqi Lu, Hongjin Qian, Di He, Zheng Liu
